name: Mathematics for ML
description: The linear algebra, calculus and probability foundations needed to understand and implement machine learning algorithms.

resources.title: Coursera: Mathematics for Machine Learning Specialization

questions.question: What is the dot product of the vectors [1, 2, 3] and [4, 5, 6]?
If matrix A is 3x2 and matrix B is 2x4, what is the shape of the product AB?
questions.explanation: The inner dimensions (2 and 2) match, and the result takes the outer dimensions: 3x4.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = 3x^2 + 2x with respect to x?
questions.explanation: Using the power rule: d/dx(3x^2) = 6x and d/dx(2x) = 2.

questions.question: In gradient descent, why do we update parameters in the direction of the negative gradient?
options: Because the gradient points toward the global minimum
Because it keeps the parameters positive
Because the gradient points in the direction of steepest increase, so its negative locally decreases the loss fastest
Because it guarantees convergence in one step
questions.explanation: The gradient gives the direction of steepest ascent; stepping opposite to it locally reduces the loss.

questions.question: For a square matrix A, if Av = 5v for a non-zero vector v, what are v and 5?
options: v is an eigenvector of A and 5 is its eigenvalue
v is the determinant of A and 5 is its trace
v is a row of A and 5 is its rank
v is the inverse of A and 5 is its norm
questions.explanation: By definition, a non-zero v with Av = lambda v is an eigenvector, and lambda is the corresponding eigenvalue.

questions.question: A test for a disease has 99% sensitivity and 99% specificity, and 1% of the population has the disease. If a random person tests positive, what is the probability they have the disease?

practical.title: Compute one gradient descent step
practical.instructions: The loss is L(w) = (w - 3)^2. Starting from w = 1 with learning rate 0.1, compute one gradient descent step. Write the derivative dL/dw, the gradient value at w = 1, and the updated value of w.
practical.expected_output: dL/dw = 2(w - 3); at w = 1 the gradient is -4; w_new = 1 - 0.1 * (-4) = 1.4

rubric.description: Uses the update rule w - lr * gradient
rubric.hint: The update rule is w_new = w - learning_rate * gradient.

tasks.title: Review vectors and matrices
tasks.description: Complete the Khan Academy units on vectors, matrix multiplication and linear transformations. Focus on dot products and how matrix shapes combine.
tasks.completion_criteria: Completes the unit exercises with at least 80% accuracy.

tasks.title: Implement vector and matrix operations in NumPy
tasks.description: Write small Python functions for dot product, matrix multiplication and transpose by hand, then compare your results with NumPy's built-in functions on random inputs.
tasks.completion_criteria: Hand-written functions match NumPy results on at least 5 test cases.

tasks.title: Derive and code gradient descent
tasks.description: Study partial derivatives and gradients, then derive the gradient of mean squared error for linear regression. Implement gradient descent from scratch and plot the loss over iterations.
tasks.completion_criteria: From-scratch gradient descent converges to within 1% of the closed-form least-squares solution.

tasks.title: Implement PCA from scratch
tasks.description: Using eigendecomposition of the covariance matrix, implement PCA from scratch on a real dataset. Compare explained variance with scikit-learn's PCA and write up the math behind each step.
tasks.completion_criteria: Explained variance ratios match scikit-learn to 3 decimal places and the write-up explains eigenvectors and variance.
